nodes.label: 2026-08-13-person-support-path.md — the person support path as built: a fourth support path in artefact_v1.py that resolves the names a question writes to person ids through the corpus's own directories, jumps to their chunks in herb-eval-v2's entity layer, and scores them like a stated fact. Ships at HERB_W_PERSON=1.0, on. Separates DECIDED (his words, cited) from OPEN (his ruling needed); every number carries the method that produced it ([CORPUS] read-only parse of v3/data/corpus/Salesforce__HERB, [DB] read-only Cypher on herb-eval-v2, [CODE] source by file and symbol). questions.jsonl and every arm_outputs.jsonl stayed closed.

The path is a fourth base, summed like the other three, and it is a weight, never a gate. Three paths existed — tag areas, description lookups, stated scope — accumulating totals[cid] += W_TAG/W_DESC/W_SCOPE * s in artefact_v1.py · _retrieve. Person matching was nominally part of stated scope through the employee_id chunk field, which exists on 30 of 4,869 chunks [DB], all 30 metadata-mirror chunks and no content chunk, so it reached nothing. A chunk with no named person still competes on tag, description and stated scope exactly as before.

The mechanism end to end. 1 Read the query: resolve_persons(text, directory) reads person names and ids off the question text deterministically — no model call, no embedding, no fuzzy distance — and the question text is the input on both legs, not the interpreter's reading of it. 2 Resolve to ids through metadata/employee.json and metadata/customers_data.json; the directories stay outside the graph and only ids are ever queried. 3 Jump to the person: one Cypher per resolved mention (_PERSON_CHUNKS_CYPHER), (p:Person {id: pid})<-[r:INVOLVES|MENTIONS]-(c:Chunk), under the same empty-chunk, dataset and excluded-section guards every other retrieval query carries. 4 Score it like a stated fact: the mention's chunk set is its pool, no clustering, base from the same fuzzy multi-k support over description distances the stated-scope path uses with extend=True; bases fold across mentions through _agg and reach the shared scale through _normalize, then totals[cid] += W_PERSON * s.

Two factors apply over the normalized base and the ordering is load-bearing: the fraction of the query's named persons a chunk carries — the path's one priority modifier, run through _mod with exposed strength HERB_STR_PERSON_MATCH as base × (1 + s·(m − 1)) — and the weight of the chunk's best kind of link, a bare per-chunk factor with no strength knob, multiplying beside HERB_W_PERSON. A weight folded into the raw base cannot damp: min-max is relative, so a pool scaled uniformly by 0.0 becomes a single scale point and _norm_pool maps every member to 1.0, the pool maximum. Applied over the normalized base, a role weight of 0.0 takes the contribution away, 0.5 halves it, 1.0 leaves it whole.

What the path never does: it adds no chunk to `semantic`, so it never sets the curve walk's K; it does not count toward the flat regime's widening gate (tag_reached); and no chunk is ever removed from the pool or the ranking by it. A chunk the path reaches at a role weight of 0.0 still enters the pool and still ranks, carrying no person contribution.

Where 'it can only add' stops holding: HERB_NORM_SCOPE=global. Under the default per_path each path min-maxes over its own pool, so the person path cannot touch another path's numbers. Under global all four bases share one min/max, and the person and scope bases are raw extend=True supports two to three orders of magnitude larger than a tag support, so adding the person path compresses the other paths toward zero. Measured on the test fixture: path off {c-tag: 1.0}; path on {c-p1: 1.0, c-tag: 0.0388}. A property of global and of any large-scale path under it — stated scope does the same today.

The resolution rule: tiers in order, a span claimed by one tier is never matched again, so one surface is one mention, and the rule that matched is recorded per mention. id_literal — \beid_[0-9a-f]{8}\b, \bEMP_\d{6,12}\b, \bCUST-\d+\b written in the query in its own case and width; exact — a directory name matched as whole tokens as the directory spells it; normalized — the same match where only case or separators differ; reordered (near tier) — the name's own tokens in the other order (Taylor, Hannah); initial (near tier) — an initial and the name's last token, resolving to every entry with that initial; ambiguous — a name several entries carry under HERB_PERSON_AMBIGUOUS=none, recorded, resolving to no id; unresolved — a token in an id's shape that is not that id, or two capitalized words the directory does not carry, recorded so a run says what it could not resolve.

What counts as an initial: a single letter, written upper case, and either carrying its own full stop or not being one of the two single-letter English words (a, i). Without that rule the tier reads the article and the pronoun as initials — against the real directory, 'Did a Brown review the PR?' resolved to 4 real employee ids and 'I Brown said so' to 3, and each phantom mention also damped every genuine mention's match fraction. A. Taylor and I. Brown still resolve; a Brown, A Taylor and I Brown do not. Id matching stays case-sensitive, but a token in an id's shape the case-sensitive tier did not claim (EID_792D7501, cust-0001) is recorded as unresolved so a miscased id leaves an audit trail instead of silence. Tokens are maximal runs of letters and digits with the underscore excluded, so an id can never be read as a name; no surname-only match, no substring match, no edit distance, no embedding.

The directories [CORPUS]: metadata/employee.json 530 entries keyed eid_… each carrying a name; metadata/customers_data.json 120 entries each carrying id (CUST-####) and a name; 650 ids; 201 distinct names (98 carried by employees, 109 by customers, 6 by both); every one of the 650 names is exactly 2 tokens; ids per name median 2, mean 3.23, max 11, with 99 of 201 names carrying exactly one id; first-name vocabulary 26 and surname vocabulary 24 across both directories, disjoint. The consequence that shapes the path: HERB spells 530 employees with 98 distinct names, 92 of them shared — 524 of the 530 employees share their full name with at least one other person, so name-to-id resolution for an employee is ambiguous by construction. Customer names are near-unique, 109 distinct names over 120 ids. Because the first-name and surname vocabularies are disjoint, the reordered form cannot collide with a different real name.

The resolver on the directory it reads [CORPUS]: round trip 201/201 — each directory name written as the directory spells it inside a neutral probe sentence resolves to exactly one mention under rule exact whose ids are exactly that name's directory ids. Written Last, First: 201/201 under reordered. Written F. Last with the full stop: 201/201 under initial. Written F Last with no full stop: 169/201 — the 32 that do not are the names whose initial is A or I, the price of not reading the article and the pronoun as initials. With HERB_PERSON_NEAR=0 both forms fall through to unresolved and nothing else moves.

The resolver on a probe bank of the corpus's own text [CORPUS]. The chunk-description probe bank HERB_DEMAND=centred uses exists only as vectors — the description text lives in herb-eval-backup, which is not on this machine (SHOW DATABASES → herb-eval, herb-eval-v2, neo4j, system) — so extraction was measured on the corpus's own declared content leaves instead, stated in the ledger rather than papered over. Bank: 42,774 declared content leaves across the 30 product files. Leaves resolving at least one person: 11,404 = 26.7%. Mentions by rule: id_literal 14,167 · exact 9,139 · reordered 0 · initial 0 · unresolved 43,587. Ids per resolved mention median 1, mean 3.13. The near tier fires zero times on 42,774 leaves of natural prose — a fact about corpus prose that bounds nothing about question-shaped text. The 26.7% is over corpus content, not over questions, and is not evidence about retrieval.

The graph the path reads [DB, herb-eval-v2]: Person 5,233 — eid 514, emp 4,590, cust 120, malformed 9; INVOLVES 32,281 — speaker 13,690, participant 9,964, reviewer 4,349, pr_author 3,492, doc_author 786; MENTIONS 9,634; chunks carrying at least one person edge 4,737 of 4,869 = 97.3% (against 30 = 0.6% through employee_id); chunks in an excluded section carrying a person edge 0; directory ids with a Person node 632 of 650, the other 18 being employees who never appear in a structured field, and a resolved id with no node reaches nothing and costs nothing. Reach per resolved id: eid median 50 chunks, mean 57.2, max 177; cust median 8, min 2, max 22.

Reachability bias — what a name can reach at all. No directory name resolves to an EMP_ id (that population is directory-less; only a query writing the id literally reaches it). Share of each role's edges a directory-resolvable name can reach [DB]: doc_author 786/786 100.0% · participant 9,964/9,964 100.0% · mentions 9,632/9,634 100.0% · speaker 13,006/13,690 95.0% · reviewer 2,053/4,349 47.2% · pr_author 1,197/3,492 34.3%. 4,696 of the 4,737 person-linked chunks (99.1%, 96.4% of the corpus) are reachable by a name. Role weights would therefore be tuned on a biased subsample — two thirds of the pr_author links and half of the reviewer links can only be reached by a query writing an EMP_ id — and that does not change until the EMP_ population is name-resolvable, which it cannot be since HERB ships no directory for it.

Reach per name, the union over the ids one mention opens: median 21 chunks = 0.43% of the corpus. The 92 names only employees carry reach a median of 256 chunks (max 566); the 103 names only customers carry reach a median of 9 (max 24); the 6 names both directories carry reach 121–557. The path is sharp for a customer name and blunt for an employee name, and the reason is the directory's own name reuse, not the graph. Cost [DB]: the arm's own person Cypher driven with a real 1024-dim need vector takes 15 ms for a single-id customer name (3 chunks) and 93 ms median for the widest employee name (10 ids, 431 chunks), one query per resolved mention; a whole _retrieve at k=50 with one employee name resolved ran in 0.89 s, the person path adding 176 chunks to the union that no other path had reached.

Flags and defaults [CODE], all reaching RETRIEVAL_FLAGS so a run manifest states the value model it ran under (33 entries, 34 on the det leg): HERB_W_PERSON 1.0 — the path's weight and its switch, starting where HERB_W_TAG / HERB_W_DESC / HERB_W_SCOPE start; at 0.0 nothing runs and below 0.0 it fails loud at import. HERB_STR_PERSON_MATCH 1.0. HERB_PERSON_AMBIGUOUS all. HERB_PERSON_NEAR 1. HERB_W_ROLE_SPEAKER / PARTICIPANT / REVIEWER / PR_AUTHOR / DOC_AUTHOR / MENTIONS each 1.0. Every one is a row in v3/CONSTANTS.md with its provenance. What a uniform role weight does, so nobody sweeps a no-op: the six weights multiply the normalized base and W_PERSON multiplies the same product, so setting all six to w is exactly HERB_W_PERSON = w × W_PERSON — the same knob twice. Only the ratios between roles say anything HERB_W_PERSON cannot, and a uniform 0.0 is the path switched off.

Fail-loud, not silent. With HERB_W_PERSON > 0 against a graph carrying no Person nodes, prepare_over_corpus names the database and stops before a question is answered — which is what a default run against herb-eval does, since build_entity_graph.py refuses herb-eval as a write target and the layer lives only in herb-eval-v2. A person edge role outside the weight map fails loud rather than scoring at an invented weight. A missing directory file fails loud, and so does resolving with no directory loaded. A negative HERB_W_PERSON, or any negative role weight, fails loud at import naming the knob.

DECIDED, his words cited: no gates — a signal weights and ranks, it never excludes ("gate? wtf? why have a gate? … hard filter seems insane, much better to use rankings etc", 07-15, turns:L729; tags "INFORM/weight", 08-01, turns:L4098). Entity fields become nodes, to get actual use of the graph (08-12). Ids only in the graph; names resolve outside it (08-12) — the security constraint this path is built under. Build the person support path, "with the same careful concept in mind" (08-13). The four path weights start at the same value, so the person path ships at 1.0 and on ("why shouldnt they all start at the same?" / "fucking nail the 1.0 start", 08-13). No content in the graph (07-06, turns:L538).

OPEN — his ruling needed. 1 HERB_W_PERSON's value beyond the 1.0 start; no run has been fired with the path on. 2 Role weights — whether speaker, participant, reviewer, PR author and document author are worth the same; shipped uniform. 3 Whether a MENTIONS link counts equal to an INVOLVES link; shipped equal, 9,634 mention edges against 32,281 structured ones. 4 Ambiguity policy — all ships on the measured ground that none retires the employee half of the path (92 of 98 employee names shared); damping by how many people a name admits is a third option nobody has ruled on and it is not built. 5 The near tier, on by default. 6 Company names — customers_data.json carries a company per customer, 10 distinct companies over 120 contacts; not built. 7 The two-hop shape (c1)-[:INVOLVES]->(p)<-[:INVOLVES]-(c2), in the entity design §2.4, not built here. 8 Whether the path runs at all in a reported configuration, and on which graph: every standing number is herb-eval and this path needs herb-eval-v2.

Assumptions ledger. UNVERIFIED — the extraction was not measured on the chunk-description probe bank; that bank's text is not on this machine (only its vectors, as Chunk.desc_emb; herb-eval-backup is absent). UNVERIFIED — no retrieval run exists with the path on; every measurement is of the resolver, the graph, and one _retrieve call on a synthetic question, and the verifying trial is not authorized by the document. ASSUMED — a query writes an id in the case the corpus writes it (eid_… lowercase, CUST- uppercase). ASSUMED — names are ASCII. VERIFIED-BY-CONSTRUCTION — the path changes nothing at weight 0: test_artefact_v1_persons.py asserts a session that raises on the person query completes untouched, rows and whole meta identical whether or not mentions are supplied, no person cell in the door trace; test_artefact_v1.py's 160 checks and the person suite's 53 pass together at the 1.0 default and under HERB_W_PERSON=0, HERB_W_PERSON=2.5, HERB_PERSON_NEAR=0, HERB_PERSON_AMBIGUOUS=none and HERB_W_ROLE_MENTIONS=0.25.
